# Notes to the Financial Statements For the year ended December 31, 2015

## I Introduction to the Bank

The Longjiang Bank Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the "the Bank") is a joint-stock commercial bank registered and incorporated in China after the approval of "Reply to the Opening of Longjiang Bank Co., Ltd. of Heilongjiang Regulatory Bureau of the China Banking Regulatory Commission" (Hei Yin Jian Fu [2009] No. 309) on December 22, 2009.

According to the promoters' agreement entered into by the promoters of the bank, the bank inherited all assets and liabilities of the Daqing City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., the Qiqihar City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Mudanjiang City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. and Qitaihe City Urban Credit Cooperatives Co., Ltd. (collectively referred to as the "four banks or cooperatives"); the relevant business was transferred to the bank on December 22, 2009.

The Bank was approved by the China Banking Regulatory Commission (hereinafter referred to as the CBRC), holding a financial license with the number of B1056H223010001, and received the business license for the enterprise's legal person with the registration number of 230000100069419 approved by the Heilongjiang Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce.

The main business of the Bank and its subsidiaries (hereinafter referred to as the "the Group") includes RMB and foreign currency deposits and loans, payment and settlement and other banking services, as well as other business approved by China Banking Regulatory Commission.

On December 31, 2015, the Bank has 13 branches, providing the retail and corporate banking services in Heilongjiang Province.

The financial statements are presented in RMB yuan, which is also the functional currency of the Bank and its subsidiaries.

## II Preparation Basis of the Financial Statements

The Group executes the Accounting Standards for Enterprises and Related Regulations issued by the Ministry of Finance of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Ministry of Finance") on February 15, 2006 and its amendments afterwards (hereinafter referred to as "Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises").

## IV The Significant Accounting Policies and Accounting Estimates 1. Accounting Year

The Group's accounting year is the gregorian calendar year, that is, from January 1 until December 31.

2. Recording Currency

The RMB is the currency in the primary economic environment in which Group operates. The Group uses the RMB as the recording currency. The Group's currency used in the preparing the financial statement is RMB.

3. Basis of Accounting and Valuation Principles

The Group's financial accounting is based on the accrual basis, except for certain financial instruments which are measured at fair value; the financial statements use historical cost as the basis of measurement. If the assets are impaired, corresponding provision for impairment shall be made in accordance with the relevant provisions.

4.Accounting Treatment Method for Business Combination Under Common Control and Under Non-Common Control

The business combination is divided into the business combination under common control and the business combination under non-common control. The Group's business combinations are business combination under non-common control.

The business combination under non-common control

Enterprises involved in the combination are not subject to the ultimate control of the same party or the identical multi-party before and after the combination, which is the business combination under non-common control.

The cost of the combination refers to the fair value of the assets paid by the buyer to obtain the seller's control right, the liabilities incurred or assumed, and the issued equity instruments. The audit, legal services, evaluation and consulting and other intermediary costs and other related administrative expenses incurred by the buyer in a business combination are included in the profit or loss at the time of occurrence. Through multiple transactions, for the enterprises, with the step-by-step realization of business combination under non-common control, the merger costs are the combination of the consideration on the purchase date and

the fair value on the purchase date of the seller's stock equity held before the date of purchase. For the seller's stock equity held prior to the date of purchase, re-measurement is conducted in accordance with fair value on the acquisition date. The difference between fair value and book value are included in investment income in the current period; for the seller's stock equity held prior to the date of purchase which involves other comprehensive income, other comprehensive income related to the current investment income on the purchase date.

The identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities determined by the buyer to meet the conditions obtained by the buyer in the combination, shall be measured at fair value on the date of purchase. If the combination cost is greater than the difference of the fair value share of identifiable net assets obtained in the combination, of the seller, it shall be recognized as goodwill and begin the initial measurement according to cost. If the combination cost is lower than the difference of the fair value share of identifiable net assets obtained in the combination, first recheck the fair value and combination cost of identifiable assets, liabilities and contingent liabilities, and if, after the recheck, the combination cost is still lower than the difference of the fair value share of identifiable net assets obtained in the combination, it will be included in the current profit and loss.

5. Goodwill

The goodwill which is formed due to the acquisition business is presented separately in the consolidated financial statements and measured at the amounts obtained after the cost less accumulated impairment. Goodwill is tested for impairment at least at the end of each year.

Impairment testing of goodwill is conducted together with the related asset group or combination of asset groups. That is, from the acquisition date, the book value of goodwill, in accordance with reasonable basis, is apportioned into asset group or combination of asset groups which can benefit from the enterprise combination, for example, the recoverable amount of asset group or combination of asset groups containing the apportion goodwill is less than its book value, recognize the corresponding impairment loss. The amount of the impairment loss is first set off against the goodwill book value apportioned to the asset group or combination of asset groups, then set off against the book value of other assets in proportion according to the proportion of the book value of other assets excluding the goodwill in the assets groups or combination of asset groups.

The recoverable amount is either the net amount of the asset's fair value less disposal costs or the present value of the expected future cash flows, and the higher one shall prevail. The fair value of assets is determined based on the sale agreement price in the fair trade; if there is no sale agreement but an active market of assets, the fair value shall be determined according to the price offered by the buyer of the asset; if there is no sale agreement or an active market of assets, the fair value of the asset shall be assessed in accordance with the best retrievable information; the disposal costs, including legal fees for asset-related disposal, related taxes, handling charges, as well as the direct costs incurred to bring the asset to its sale condition. The present value of the assets expected future cash flows, according to the expected future cash flows generated in continued use and ultimate disposal of the assets, select the appropriate discount rate to determine in accordance with discounted amount.

Goodwill impairment loss is included in the current profit or loss when it occurs, and shall not be reversed in future accounting periods.

### 6. Criterion for Determination of Cash and Cash Equivalents

Cash refers to the cash on hand and the deposit which are readily available for payment. Cash equivalents are investment held by the Group which is short-term, highly liquid, and readily convertible to known amounts of cash, with insignificant risk of change in value.

### 7. Financial Instruments

A financial asset or financial liability is recognized when the Group becomes a party to the contract of financial instruments. Financial assets and financial liabilities are measured at fair value at initial recognition. For financial assets and financial liabilities measured at fair value and its changes included in the current profit or loss, related transaction costs are directly included in the profit or loss, for financial assets and financial liabilities of the other categories, related transaction costs are included the amount initially recognized.

#### (1) The determining method for the fair value

Fair value refers to the price that can be received from selling one asset or needs to be paid from transferring one liability during the orderly transactions of market participants at the measurement date. No matter fair value is observable or appraised by appraisal technology, the fair value measured and disclosed in this financial statement is confirmed on such basis.

As for the financial assets and financial liabilities that are consecutively measured on fair value, the Group divides the financial tools into three tiers based on the observability of input fair value and the importance of such input to the whole measurement of fair value as follows:

Tier One: The measurement of fair value refers to the offer of same assets or liabilities that can be obtained but is not adjusted on the active market at the measurement date;

Tier Two: The measurement of fair value refers to the input value of relevant assets or liabilities that can be directly or indirectly observable except the input value of Tier One;

Tier Three: The measurement of fair value refers to the input value of relevant assets or liabilities that cannot be observable.

If the financial tool exists on the active market, the Group adopts the offer on the active market as the fair value.

The active market offer of financial tool refers to the price that is easily obtained from the Exchanges, industrial associations, pricing service institutions or supervision institutions and represents the market transaction price actually and frequently occurs during the fair transactions. If the above conditions cannot be met, it shall be considered as non-active market. The signs of non-active market mainly include the existence of obvious bid-ask spread, obvious enlarging of bid-ask spread and non-existence of recent transaction.

If the financial tool does not have any active market, the Group determines the fair value by the appraisal technologies. Appraisal technologies include the reference of the price used during the recent market transactions among each party in similar situations, the reference of current fair value of other materially same financial tools, the discounted cash flow technique, the option pricing model, etc.

#### (2) The effective interest method

The effective interest method is the method to calculate amortized cost and interest income or expense in various periods in accordance with the effective interest rate of the financial assets or financial liabilities (including a group of financial assets or financial liabilities). The actual interest rate refers to the future cash flows of a financial asset or financial liability in the expected duration or within the applicable shorter period, is discounted into the interest rates used in the current book value for financial assets or financial liabilities.

In calculating the effective interest rate, the Group will consider the expected future cash flows on the basis of all the terms of the contract of the financial assets or financial liabilities (not consider future credit losses), and will also consider the fees and charges, transaction fees and discount or premium paid or received by the contracted parties of the financial assets or financial liabilities, which belongs to the effective interest rate components.

Upon initial recognition, the financial assets are classified as financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, held-to-maturity investments, loans and receivables and available-for-sale financial assets. Regular way purchases of financial assets are recognized and derecognized on a trade date basis.

#### (3) Classification, recognition and measurement of financial assets

 $ \underline{\text{Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss}} $

Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss include held-for-trading financial assets and financial assets designated as financial assets at fair value through profit or loss.

Trading financial assets refer to the financial assets meeting one of the following conditions:

● The purpose of obtaining the financial asset is mainly aimed for selling in the near future;

● Upon initial recognition, they are part of identifiable portfolio of financial instruments under centralized management, and there is objective evidence indicating that the Group's recently adopts a pattern of short-term profit-taking for the portfolio management;

The financial assets meeting one of the following conditions, at initial recognition, can be designated as financial assets at fair value through profit or loss:

● The designation may eliminate or significantly reduce inconsistency of the related gains or losses in the measurement or recognition resulting from the different basis of measurement of the financial assets;

● The formal written document of the Group's risk management or investment strategy has set out, the portfolio of financial assets or financial assets and financial liabilities portfolio where the financial asset belongs to shall be managed and evaluated based on the fair value, and be reported to the key management personnel

Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss shall adopt the fair value for follow-up measurement, and the gains or losses from changes in fair value, as well as dividends and interest income related to such financial assets shall be included in the current profit or loss.

##### Held-to-maturity investments

The held-to-maturity investments refer to non-derivative financial assets with fixed maturity, fixed or determinable recovery amount, which the Group has the positive intention and ability to hold to maturity.

The hold-to-maturity investment uses the effective interest method and is subsequently measured at amortized cost; the gains or losses arising from derecognition, impairment or amortization shall be included in the current profit or loss.

##### Loans and receivables

Loans and receivables are non-derivative financial assets which are not quoted in an active market, with fixed or determinable recovery amount. The financial assets that the Group divides as loans and receivables include funds deposited in central banks, interbank placement, call loan to banks or other financial agency, redemptory financial assets for sale, interest receivable, loans and advances, investment in receivables and other receivables, and so on.

Loans and receivables are subsequently measured at amortized cost using the effective interest method, and the gains or losses arising from derecognition, impairment or amortization shall be included in the current profit or loss

#### Available—for—sale financial assets

Available—for—sale financial assets are non-derivative financial assets designated as available for sale at initial recognition and financial assets other than the financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, loans and receivables, and held-to-maturity investment.

Available—for—sale financial assets are subsequently measured at fair value, and the gain or loss from changes in fair value, except for impairment losses and the exchange differences between foreign currency monetary financial assets and amortized cost included in the current profit or loss, is recognized as other comprehensive income, and transferred when the financial asset is derecognized, which shall be included in the current profit or loss.

The interest obtained during the period when the available for sale financial assets are held and the cash dividends declared by invested entity, shall be respectively included in interest income and investment income.

In active market, the equity instrument that has no offer and whose fair value can't be measured reliably shall be measured by the cost subtracting the confirmed impairment loss at the end of report period.

#### (4) Impairment of financial assets

In addition to the financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, the Group carries out the check for the carrying value of other financial assets on each balance sheet date. If there is objective evidence indicating that financial assets are impaired, impairment provision shall be made. The objective evidence showing the impairment of financial assets are the matters which actually happens after the financial assets are initially recognized, affects the expected future cash flows of the financial assets and the impact of which the enterprises can reliably measure.

The objective evidence of impairment of financial assets includes the following matters that can be observed:

● The issuer or obligor encounters serious financial difficulties;

● The obligor has breach of contract terms, such as a default or overdue in interest or principal payments;

● The Group makes concessions for a debtor in financial difficulty, due to economic or legal considerations;

● It is probable that the debtor will enter bankruptcy or make other financial reorganization;

● Disappearance of an active market for that financial asset because of financial difficulties;

● It is unable to identify whether an asset's cash flow in a group of financial assets has been reduced, however, based on public data, we have found that, after overall evaluation, the expected future cash flows of the group of financial assets have really been reduced and measureable since the initial recognition, including:

– The gradual deterioration of the financial assets debtor's ability to pay;

-- The debtor country or regional economic situation that may lead to the Group of financial assets can not be paid;

● The technology, market, economic or legal environment at the equity instruments issuer's business place has the material adverse change, which makes its investor in equity instruments may not be able to recover the investment costs;

● The fair value of equity instruments investment has a significant or Non-transient decline;

#### ● Other objective evidence indicates the financial assets impairment.

#### Impairment of financial assets measured at amortized cost

The Group separately conducts the impairment tests for individually significant financial assets; conduct the impairment tests for individually not significant financial assets, or conducts the impairment tests included in the portfolios of financial assets with similar credit risk characteristics. After the independent test, the financial assets with no impairment (including individually significant or not significant financial assets) is tested for impairment included in the portfolios of financial assets with similar credit risk characteristics. The financial assets whose impairment losses are identified in individual impairment test are not tested for impairment loss in the portfolios of financial assets with similar credit risk characteristics.

For the financial assets measured at the cost or amortized cost, its book value is reduced to expected future cash flow value discounted at the financial asset's original effective interest rate (excluding future credit risk which has not yet occurred), the reduced amount is recognized as an impairment loss, which shall be included in the current profit and loss. After the impairment loss of the financial asset is recognized, if there is objective evidence indicating that the value of financial assets has been restored, and it is objectively related to the matter occurred after the loss is confirmed, the previously recognized impairment loss shall be reversed to the extent the book value of the financial asset after the impairment loss is reversed does not exceed what the amortized cost would have been on the reversal date had the impairment not been recognized.

#### Available—for—sale financial assets impairment

Where available—for—sale financial asset is impaired, the cumulative loss due to the decline in fair value which is originally included in capital surplus shall be transferred and included in the current profit and loss. The amount of the cumulative loss of such transfer is the initial acquisition costs of the assets less the retrieved principal and amortization payment, and the current fair value and the balance included in profit or loss after the impairment loss.

After the impairment loss is recognized, if there is objective evidence indicating that the value of financial assets has been restored, and objectively relates to the matter occurred after the loss is confirmed, the previously recognized impairment loss is reversed, and available—for—sale equity instrument impairment losses reversal is recognized as other comprehensive income and included in the capital reserve, the available—for—sale debt instruments impairment loss is reversed and included in the current profit and loss.

#### Financial assets impairment measured at cost

For the equity instruments impairment which is not quoted in an active market and whose fair value can not be reliably measured, the impairment loss amount is the difference between the carrying value of financial assets and the present value determined for the future cash flows discounted at the prevailing market rate of return for similar financial assets. The impairment losses of such financial assets, once recognized, are not reversed.

## (5) Derecognition of financial assets

The Group derecognizes financial assets meeting one of the following conditions:

● Termination of the contractual rights to receive the cash flows of such financial assets;

● The financial assets have been transferred, and almost all of the risks and rewards concerning the ownership of financial assets have been transferred to the transferee;

● The financial assets have been transferred, and the Group waives control over the financial assets, although it has neither transferred nor retained almost all of the risks and rewards concerning the ownership of financial assets.

If the Group has neither transferred nor retained almost all of the risks and rewards concerning the ownership of financial assets, nor give up control over the financial assets, the Group recognizes the financial assets to the extent of its continuing involvement in transferred financial assets, and recognizes the corresponding liabilities. The extent of continuing involvement in transferred financial assets refers to the level of risk facing the enterprise due to the changes in the value of financial assets.

If an entire financial asset transfer qualifies for derecognition, the difference between carrying amount of the transferred financial assets and the sum of the considerations received from the transfer and the cumulative change amount of the fair value originally recognized in other comprehensive income changes shall be included in the current profit or loss.

## (6) Classification, recognition and measurement of financial liabilities

## The classification and measurement of financial liabilities

The Group recognizes the issued financial instruments as financial liabilities or equity instruments based on the essence of a contractual arrangement of the financial instruments and the definition of financial liabilities and equity instruments.

### Financial liabilities

Financial liabilities are subsequently measured at amortized cost using the effective interest method, and the gains or losses arising from derecognition or amortization are included in the current profit or loss.

#### Equity instruments

An equity instrument refers to any contract that evidences a residual interest in the assets of the Group after deduction of all liabilities. The Group's issued equity instruments are recognized at the proceeds received, net of direct issue costs.

## (7) Derecognition of financial liabilities

The Group derecognizes financial liabilities only when its present obligation has been discharged, canceled or expires. The Group (the debtor) and creditors shall sign an agreement to replace the existing financial liability by taking on new financial liability method, and in case the new financial liabilities and contractual terms of the existing financial liabilities are substantially different, the Group shall derecognize the existing financial liability, and at the same time recognize the new financial liabilities.

On derecognition of a financial liability in its entirety, the Group shall have the difference between the carrying amount of financial liabilities and paid considerations (including non-cash assets transferred or new financial liabilities assumed) included in the current profit and loss.

## (8) Financial guarantee contracts

Financial guarantee contracts require the issuer to provide repayment protection for the contract holders, that is, on behalf of the contract holder to pay his loss when the guaranteed person can not fulfill the due payments within the terms of the contract.

The financial guarantee contracts managed by the Group according to the fair value shall be designated to be financial liabilities at fair value through profit or loss upon initial recognition. Such financial guarantee contracts are recognized at fair value, changes in fair value at re-measurement shall be included in the current profit or loss.

The financial guarantee contracts which are not designated as financial liabilities at fair value through profit or loss are recognized at fair value at initial recognition and are subsequently measured at the amount determined in accordance with the "Accounting Standards for Enterprises No. 13-Contingencies" and the initially recognized amount less the accumulated amortization determined in accordance with the principle of "Accounting Standards for Enterprises No. 14-Revenue" whichever is higher.

## (9) The offsetting of financial assets and financial liabilities

When the Group has offset the recognized statutory rights to the financial assets and financial liabilities, and the statutory rights are executable at present, and the Group plans to make the net settlement or simultaneous realization of the financial asset and settle the financial liabilities, the amount after financial assets and financial liabilities offset each other shall be listed in the balance sheet. In addition, financial assets and financial liabilities are presented separately in the balance sheet, without offsetting.

### 8. The Long-term Equity Investments

Control means that the investor obtains the rights against the investee, enjoys variable return by taking part in related activities of the investee and is capable of making use of his rights against the investee to affect the amount of his return. Joint control refers to the control jointly owned of an arrangement according to relevant stipulations, and the arranged relevant activity must be determined under unanimous consent of participants who sharing control power. Significant influence means that someone has the right to participate in decision-making of a company's financial and operating policies, but is unable to control or jointly control with other parties the formulation of these policies. When determining whether the investee is able to be controlled or significantly influenced, we have considered the convertible company bonds in current period, exercisable warrants in current period and other potential voting rights factors held by the investor and other parties.

Long-term equity investment shall be initially measured at its cost. For the long-term equity investment gained from business combination under non-common control, the combined cost at the acquisition date is taken as the initial invested capital of the long-term equity investment.

Save for the long-term equity investment formed in the business combination, the long-term equity investment acquired by other means is initially measured at its cost. For long-term equity investment that is able to make significant influence on or conduct joint control rather than control over the invested entity, its cost is the fair value of the original held equity investment that is determined according to No. 22 of Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises – Recognition and Measurement of Financial Instruments.

### Long-term equity investment checked using the cost method

The Group calculates the long-term equity investment of the subsidiary with cost method. A subsidiary refers to the invested subject that can be controlled by the Group.

When cost method is used, the long-term equity investment is measured at the initial investment cost. Additional investment or disinvestment can adjust the cost of the long-term equity investment. Save for the cost actually paid when the investment is obtained or the cash dividends or profits that are included in the consideration but not yet issued, the investment profits in the current period are determined as the cash dividends or profits that the invested entity declares to issue.

#### The long-term equity investment checked by using the equity method

The Group's investment in associates and joint ventures shall be accounted for by using the equity method. Associates are the investee on which the Group is able to exert a significant impact and a joint venture refers to the investee over which the Group and other investors have their joint control.

When using the equity method accounting, if the initial outlay cost of the long-term equity investment is greater than the fair value share of identifiable net assets of investment unit which should be given when investment, the initial outlay cost of the long-term equity investment shall not be adjusted. Otherwise, the difference will be included in the current profits and losses and the cost of the long-term equity investment will be adjusted simultaneously.

In calculation with equity method, investment profits and losses in current period are the shares of net profits and losses that shall be enjoyed and undertaken realized in current year of the invested entity. When confirming the shares of net profits and losses of the invested entity that shall be enjoyed, based on the fair value of various identifiable assets and so on of the invested entity when the investment is acquired, according to the accounting policy and accounting period of the Group, confirm after adjusting the net profits of the invested entity. For the profits and losses of unrealized internal transaction between the Group and associated and jointed enterprises, the part of the Group is calculated according to shareholding ratio and offset, based on which the investment profits and losses will be determined. However, the loss of the unrealized internal transaction between the Group and the invested entity that belongs to the impairment loss of the transferred assets shall not be offset. For other shareholders' equity change of the invested entity except for the net profits and losses, adjust the book value of the long-term equity investment accordingly to confirm it as other comprehensive income and record in capital reserves.

When confirming the net losses of the invested entity that shall be undertaken, write down the book

value of the long-term equity investment and other long-term equities that essentially constitute the net investment of the invested entity to nothing as a limit, unless the Group is obligated to bear additional losses of the invested entity. If the invested entity realizes net profits in subsequent periods, the group shall restore the confirmed gain sharing amount after the gain sharing amount has made up the unconfirmed loss sharing amount.

### The disposal of long-term equity investment

When dealing with the long-term equity investment, the difference between its book value and the actual price shall be included in current profits or losses. For the long-term equity investments calculated with equity method, when dealing with this investment, adopt same basis that the invested entity directly disposes the underlying assets or liabilities and carries on accounting treatment accordingly towards the part that is included in other comprehensive income.

### 9. Fixed Assets

Fixed assets are tangible assets held to provide services, used for rental or management, with the service life of more than one fiscal year. Fixed assets can be recognized only when the related economic benefits are likely to flow to the Group and its cost can be reliably measured. Fixed assets are initially measured at the cost, giving consideration to the impact of expected costs of abandoning.

Subsequent expenditures related to fixed assets, if the economic benefits associated with the fixed assets is likely to flow to the Group and its cost can be reliably measured, are included in the cost of fixed assets, and derecognize the carrying value of the replaced part. The other continued spending shall be included in the current profit or loss at the time of occurrence.

Fixed assets, starting from the next month when it reaches its intended serviceable condition, use the straight-line method to calculate the depreciation over its service life. The useful life of various fixed assets and estimated net residual values and annual depreciation rate are as follows:


<table border=1 style='margin: auto; word-wrap: break-word;'><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Classes</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Useful life</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>The ratio of estimated residual values</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Annual depreciation rate</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Buildings</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>15-30 years</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>3%-5%</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>3.17%-6.47%</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Electronic equipment</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>3-5 years</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>0%-5%</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>19.00%-33.33%</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Transport tools</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>4-6 years</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>0%-5%</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>15.83%-25.00%</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Furniture and other</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>3-5 years</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>0%-5%</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>19.00%-33.33%</td></tr></table>

Expected net salvage value refers to the amount that the Group obtains from the disposal of assets after deducting the estimated costs of disposal when the assumed fixed assets' expected service life is full and in the expected state at the end of service life.

The Group shall review the service life of fixed assets, the estimated net residual values and depreciation method at least at the end of the year; if there is any change, it shall be handled as a change in accounting estimate. When the fixed assets are at disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from the use or disposal thereof, derecognition of fixed assets shall be made. The income from sale, transfer, retirement or destroy of fixed assets sales less the book value and related taxes is included in profit or loss.

### 10. Construction in Progress

Construction in progress cost shall be measured at the actual cost, and the actual costs includes the project expenditure and other related costs incurred during the construction period. Construction in progress is not depreciated. Construction in progress is transferred as fixed assets in achieving its intended use.

### 11. Intangible Assets

Intangible assets include land use rights, computer software, and core deposits.

The obtained land use rights are often accounted for as an intangible asset. For the buildings individually developed, the related land use right and buildings, construction costs shall be accounted for as intangible assets and fixed assets. For the houses and buildings obtained by outsourcing, the related cost is allocated between the land use right and buildings, if it is difficult to make the rational allocation, all shall be disposed of as fixed assets.

Intangible assets shall be initially measured at cost. The intangible assets with limited useful life, since they are available for use, their original value less estimated net salvage value, and provision for impairment accumulated amount shall adopt the equal installments amortization within their expected useful life using the straight-line method. Intangible assets with indefinite useful life are not amortized.

At the end of the term, the useful life and amortization method of intangible assets with finite useful life are reviewed, and adjustments are made when necessary.

### 12. The Foreclosed Assets

The foreclosed assets are initially measured at fair value. On the balance sheet date, the foreclosed assets shall be measured in accordance with the book value and net realizable value, and when the net realizable value is lower than the book value, provision for impairment shall be made for the foreclosed assets.

In the disposal of the foreclosed assets, the differences between the obtained disposal income and foreclosed assets book value are included in non-operating income or expense.

The obtained foreclosed assets are converted to personal use, the settlement and transfer shall be conducted according to the carrying amount of foreclosed assets on the date of conversion. For those for which the provision for impairment of the foreclosed assets has been made, the provision for impairment shall be settled and transferred at the same time.

### 13. Impairment of Non-financial Assets

The Group shall check the long-term equity investments, fixed assets, construction in progress, the intangible assets with definite service life and other assets to see if there are signs of possible impairment at each balance sheet date. If those assets have depreciation indication, then the recoverable amount is estimated. The assets' recoverable amount is estimated on an individual assets basis, if it is difficult to estimate the recoverable amount of an individual asset, on the basis of the asset group that the asset belongs, the recoverable amount of the asset group shall be determined. If the asset's recoverable amount is less than its carrying value, the provision for asset impairment shall be made according to the difference, and be included in the current profit or loss.

The recoverable amount is the higher one of the asset's fair value less net value after the disposal costs and present value of the assets' expected future cash flows. The fair value of assets shall be determined based on the price in the sale agreement in the fair trade; in case there is no sale agreement but an active market of assets, the fair value shall be determined in accordance with the buyer's price of the asset; in case that there is no sale agreement or an active market of assets, the fair value of assets is estimated on the basis of the best information. Costs of disposal include legal fees, taxes, and handling charges related to disposal of the assets, as well as the direct costs incurred by bringing the asset to the sale condition. Once an impairment loss for the above assets is recognized, it is not reversed in subsequent accounting periods.

### 14. Employee Compensation

Except for the compensation given for the cancellation of the labor relations with employees, during the accounting period when the employees render services to the Group, the remuneration payable to the employee is recognized as a liability.

Social insurance premiums

The Group is required to participate in the workers social security system established by government agencies, including the basic endowment insurance, medical insurance, housing provident funds and other social security system, and when the corresponding expenditure occurs, they shall be included in the current profit or loss.

#### Post-retirement benefits

Post-retirement benefits include early retirement benefits and supplemental retirement benefits.

The internal early retirement benefits refer to the welfare costs paid to the employees who haven't yet reached the statutory retiring age but voluntarily withdraw from the work post upon approval by the Bank's management. The Bank shall pay the early retirement benefits to employees who receive the internal early retirement in the domestic institutions since the starting date of early retirement arrangements until they reach normal retirement age required by the State.

As of balance sheet date, Post–retirement benefits obligations are acturized by the independent actuary using expected benefits unit method, and relevant newly increased service cost and interest cost will be included into the loss and profit during the occurring period. The actuarial profit or loss caused by change in actuarial assumption will be included into the loss and profit and other comprehensive incomes respectively considering internal early retirement benefits and supplementary retirement benefits during the occurring period.

15. The Transfer of Assets Attached to Repurchase Conditions

### Recoursable financial assets acquired

According to the agreement commitments, the financial assets to be resold on a specific date in the future shall not be confirmed in the balance sheet. The cost paid to buy those assets shall be listed as recoursable financial assets acquired in the balance sheet. The difference between the buying price and reselling price shall be confirmed according to effective interest method within an agreed period and included in the interest income.

## Financial assets sold for repurchase

According to the agreement commitments, the sold financial assets bought back on a specific date in the future shall not be confirmed in the balance sheet. The payment obtained by selling such assets shall be listed as the payment of the sold buy-back financial assets in the balance sheet. The difference between the selling price and repurchase price shall be confirmed according to the effective interest method and included in interest expense.

### 16. Estimated Liabilities

When the Group assumes current obligations due to a past event, and is probably to be required to settle the obligation, the Group will recognized such obligation as accrued liabilities.

The amount recognized as the accrued liabilities shall be the best estimate for the considerations to be paid for the unfulfilled current obligations at the end of each reporting period, after taking into accounts the related risks and uncertainties. If the accrued liabilities are measured according to the estimated cash flows of the expenditure required by the expected fulfillment of the current obligations, its carrying amount is the present value of such cash flows (where the effect is significant).

If part or all expected economic benefits required to outflow for the settlement of liabilities is expected to get third-party compensation, the receivables shall be recognized as the assets when the amount of compensation is basically decided to be able to receive and the receivables can be reliable measured.

### 17. Interest Income and Expense

Interest income and expense shall be calculated in accordance with the amortized cost of the related financial assets and financial liabilities using the effective interest method, and included in the current profit or loss. If the difference between the effective interest rates and contract interest rate is smaller, it may also be calculated in accordance with the contract rates.

### 18. Fee and Commission Income

Fee and commission income is recognized on an accrual basis when services are provided.

### 19. Government Grants

Government grants are monetary assets and non-monetary assets the Group obtains from the government free of charge, excluding the capital invested by the government as an owner. Government grants are divided into asset-related government grants and income-related government grants.

If the government grants are monetary assets, they shall be measured at the amount received or receivable. If the government grants are non-monetary assets, they shall be measured at fair value; if the fair value can not be reliably obtained, it shall be measured at their nominal amounts. The government grants measured according to the nominal amount shall be included directly in the current profit and loss.

Government grants related to assets shall be recognized as deferred income, and shall be equally distributed in the life of the related assets and included in the current profit or loss. Government grant related to income, if it is

used to compensate for the related costs and losses in subsequent periods, shall be recognized as deferred income, and during the period when the relevant expenses are recognized, shall be included in the current profit or loss; if it is used to compensate for the related costs and losses, it shall be included directly in the current profit or loss.

If the government subsidy that has been recognized needs to be refunded, if there is the balance of the related deferred income, it shall be offset against the carrying amount of the deferred revenue balance, the excess part shall be included in the current profit or loss; if there is no deferred income, it shall be included directly in the profit or loss.

### 20. Income Tax

Income tax expense comprises current income tax and deferred income tax.

#### Current income tax

On the balance sheet date, the current income tax liabilities (or assets) in the current and prior periods shall be measured at the expected payable (or refundable) income tax calculated according to tax laws.

#### Deferred income tax

For the difference between the carrying value of certain assets and liabilities and their tax bases, and temporary differences of the difference between book value and tax basis of the item which is not recognized as assets and liabilities but for which the tax basis can be determined in accordance with the tax law, the deferred income tax assets and deferred tax liabilities shall be recognized by using the balance sheet liability method.

Under normal circumstances, all taxable temporary differences are recognized as the related deferred income tax liabilities. For deductible temporary differences, the Group recognizes the deferred tax assets to the extent of the taxable income which is probably to be obtained to deduct the deductible temporary differences. But the taxable temporary differences related to the initial recognition of goodwill, and related to initial recognition of the assets or liabilities occurring during the taxable income (or deductible loss) not in a business combination or the occurrence that does not affect accounting profit are not recognized as deferred tax liabilities.

For the deductible losses and tax credits that may be carried forward, the corresponding deferred income tax assets shall be recognized to the extent of the probable future taxable income which is used to offset against tax losses and tax credits.

The Group recognizes deferred income tax liabilities for taxable temporary differences arising from subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures, except where the Group is able to control the timing of the reversal of

temporary differences, and that the temporary differences in the foreseeable future is unlikely to be reversed. As to the deductible temporary differences related to the subsidiaries, associates and joint ventures, only when the temporary differences in the foreseeable future is likely to be reversed, and in the future, it is likely to be used to offset the deductible temporary differences taxable income, the Group shall recognize it as the deferred income tax assets.

On the balance sheet date, the deferred income tax assets and deferred tax liabilities shall, according to tax law, be measured at the applicable tax rates during the period of the expected recovery of the related asset or settlement of the related liability.

Except that the current income tax and deferred tax related with the transaction and matters directly included in other comprehensive income or the owner's equity are included in other comprehensive income or owner's equity, as well as deferred income tax occurred in the business combination adjusts book value of goodwill, the rest of the current income tax and deferred tax expense or income are included in the current profit or loss.

On the balance sheet date, the carrying value of the deferred income tax assets is reviewed, and if in the future, it is probably to be unable to obtain the sufficient taxable income to offset the deferred income tax assets interests, it may write—off the carrying value of deferred income tax assets. It is probable that when the sufficient taxable income is obtained, the amount of write—off should be reversed.

When the Group has a statutory right of the netting, and the intent to settle by netting or acquires assets and settles the liability simultaneously, the Group's current tax assets and the current tax liabilities are carried at the net after the offset.

When the Group has the legal rights of netting settlement to the current income tax assets and current income tax liabilities, and deferred income tax assets and deferred tax liabilities are related to the income tax levied by the same taxation authority on the same taxable entity or related to different taxable entities, but during the reversal period of deferred income tax assets and liabilities with the future importance, the taxpayer involves intends to settle by netting of current tax assets and liabilities or obtain the assets and settle the liabilities at the same time, the deferred income tax assets and the deferred tax liabilities of the Group shall be listed as the net after the offset.

21. The Trustee and Agency Business

The trustee of the Group mainly includes entrusted loans and entrusted agent investment. Entrusted loans refer

to that the customers (as principal) provide funds, the Group (as trustee) in accordance with the principal object of the loans, use, amount, term, interest rates, acts as an agent to grant, supervise and use the loans, and the Group provides assistance in the recovery of loans, the risk shall be borne by such principal, the Group only charges a handling fee. The Group's actual receipt of the funds provided by the principal are included in the entrusted loan fund; when granting the loans according to principal's wishes, it shall be included in the entrusted loan in accordance with the amount actually paid or invested. Agent financial funds are provided by the principal, and the Group shall make the investment on behalf of the principal in the agreed period and the agreed scope. The Group only charges a handling fee, not to bear the major risks associated with the agent financial assets. The above agent financial assets and the maturity make the obligations of returning the assets to the principal checked outside the balance sheet.

22.Lease

The finance lease is the lease essentially transferring of all the risks and rewards related with the ownership of an asset, and its ownership may eventually be transferred or may not be transferred. The lease other than the finance leases is operating lease.

The Group as lessee records the operating lease

Operating lease rental expense shall be included in the current profit or loss on a straight-line basis over the lease periods. Initial direct costs are included in the current profit or loss. The contingent rental shall be included in the current profit or loss when it actually occurs.

The Group as a lessor records the operating lease

Operating lease rental income is recognized as the current profit and loss on a straight-line basis over the lease periods. The initial direct costs with larger amount is capitalized at the time of occurrence, within the lease period, it will be included in the current profit or loss periodically in accordance with the same basis as rental income; other initial direct costs with smaller amount are included in the current profit or loss when it occurs. The contingent rental shall be included in the current profit or loss when it actually occurs.

## 23. The Preparation Method of Consolidated Financial Statements

The consolidation scope of consolidated financial statements is determined on the basis of control. The control refers to the investor having the rights to own the investee, and to have the variable returns through participating in the relevant activities of the investee, and has the ability to use power to influence the amount of return of investee.

As to the subsidiary disposed of by the Group, the results of operations and cash flows prior to the disposal date (the date of loss of control power) have been properly included in the consolidated income statement and consolidated cash flow statement.

The principal accounting policies and accounting periods adopted by the subsidiary shall be determined in accordance with the bank's unified accounting policies and accounting periods.

If the accounting policies and accounting period adopted by the subsidiary are inconsistent with the bank, in the preparation of the consolidated financial statements, the Group has made the necessary adjustments to the financial statements of the subsidiaries in accordance with the bank's accounting policies and accounting period.

All the major accounts and transactions between the Bank and its subsidiary and between the subsidiaries shall be offset on consolidation.

The owner's equity of the subsidiary which does not belong to the parent company's share shall be listed as the "minority interest", in the consolidated balance sheet, it shall be listed as "minority interests" under the item of the owner's equity. The share in the net profit or loss of the current period of the subsidiary company which is belonging to the rights and interests of minority shareholders shall be listed under the net profit item with "minority interest income" item in the consolidated statement of income.

If the subsidiary's minority shareholders share of current losses exceeded the share enjoyed by the minority shareholders in the owner's equity in the subsidiary at the beginning, the balance still offsets the minority interests.

For the transactions with the purchase of the subsidiary's minority equity stake or disposal of part of the equity investment, but with no loss of control over the subsidiary shall be checked as an equity transaction, The adjustment shall be made to the carrying value of the parent company's owners' equity and minority interests to reflect its subsidiary interests. The difference between the minority interest adjustments and the fair value of the paid / received consideration adjust the capital surplus, if the capital surplus is not sufficient, adjust the retained earnings.

As for the loss of control over the original subsidiary due to the disposal of some equity investments or other reasons, the remaining equity shall be re-measured in accordance with its fair value on the date of loss

of control. The sum of the considerations obtained by the disposal of equity and the fair value of the remaining equity minus the difference between the share of net assets calculated according to the original shareholding ratio that should be enjoyed by continuous calculation since the purchase date of the original subsidiary price, which shall be included in the investment income of the current period of loss of control. The other comprehensive income with the original subsidiary's investment shall be converted into the current investment income of the current period at the time of loss of control rights.

## V The Important Judgments in the Application of Accounting Policies and Key Assumptions and Uncertainties Used in Accounting Estimates

The Group, during the process accounting policy described in the Note 4, due to the inherent uncertainties of the operating activities, the Group needs to judge, estimates and makes assumptions the book value of the statement items that can not be accurately measured, These judgments, estimates and assumptions are based on past historical experience of the management of the Group, and made by taking into account other relevant factors and the actual results could differ materially from the estimates of the Group.

The Group makes regularly review the aforementioned judgments, estimates and assumptions on the basis of continuing operations. The changes in Accounting Estimates affects only the period of the change, its impact is recognized in the period of the change; as for the impacts on the current period of the change and the future period, the impact amount is recognized during the current change period and the future period.

On the balance sheet date, the important areas that the Group is required to judge the book value of assets, liabilities, estimates and makes assumptions about are listed as follows:

## 1. The Loans and Advances Impairment

The Group assesses the impairment of the loan portfolio on a regular basis. The Group shall, based on the objective basis of observable data which reflect that the loan portfolio cash flow is significantly reduced, judge whether the loan portfolio has the indication of impairment. When the reduction in cash flow can not be identified in an individual form or a single loan is not significant, the management uses a combination way, estimates the future cash flows of the loan portfolio based on historical loss experience for similar assets. The Group regularly reviews the methods and assumptions used to estimate the amount and time of future cash flows, in order to reduce the difference between the estimated impairment losses on loans and actual loan impairment losses.

## 2. The Fair Value of Financial Instruments

As to the financial instruments with no active markets, the Group determines its fair value through a variety of valuation methods. These valuation methods include the discounted cash flow model analysis. The Group is required to estimate the aspects such as their own and counterparty's credit risk, the underlying assumptions change will impact the fair value of financial instruments.

## 3. Held-to-maturity Investments

The Group will categorize the non-derivative financial assets as held-to-maturity investments which comply with the conditions, have fixed or determined repayment amount and fixed maturities and that the Group has the positive intention and ability to hold to maturity. The classification of such kind requires a lot of judgment involved. During the process of making this judgment, the Group will assess the intention and ability for holding such hold-to maturity investments. In addition to the specific circumstances (for example, the sale of investment with not significant amount towards the maturity date), the Group is not able to hold such investments to maturity, it shall reclassify all of these investments as available-for-sale financial assets.

## 4. Hold-to-maturity Investments Impairment

The Group's determination of whether the hold-to-maturity investment is impaired to a large extent is dependent on the judgment of management. Objective evidence of impairment includes the serious financial difficulties of the issuer which makes the financial asset unable to continue to be traded in an active market, unable to fulfill the terms of the contract (for example, when interest or principal payments default occurs). During the process of judgment, the Group is required to assess the objective evidence of impairment and predicts the impact of future cash flows of the investment.

## 5. Available—for—sale Financial Assets Impairment

The Group's determination of whether the available—for—sale financial assets is impaired to a large extent is dependent on the judgment of management. In the process of the judgment, the Group is required to assess the extent and duration of the fair value of the investment below the cost, as well as the financial condition of the investee and short-term business outlook, including industry conditions, technological change, credit rating, default rates and counterparty risks.

## 6. Income Tax

During the Group's normal business activities, in part of the transaction, the final tax treatment and calculation has a certain uncertainty. Whether some of the projects are able to be disbursed from costs and expenses before tax requires identification of the competent authority of the Government. If there is difference between the final determination results of these tax matters with the initial amount included in the account, the difference will impact the current income tax and deferred tax in its derecognition period.

## 7. Post-retirement Benefits

The Bank, based on various assumptions, uses the expect benefit unit method to determine the post-retirement benefits liabilities. These assumptions include discount rate, the growth rate of the average medical costs, subsidy growth rate of internal retired personnel and other factors. The actual amount and the estimated amount may be different. Any differences of actual results or changes of assumptions may affect the bank's post-retirement benefits costs, other comprehensive income and the remaining balance of the liability.

## 8. Have the Judgment of Control to the Structured Subject

As the manager of the structured subject, this group is the main responsible person or the agent to make the evaluation, to determine whether the group has control to this structured subject. Based on the scope of decision of the manager, and the right held by other parties, and the remuneration got by providing manager service and faced variable gain exposure to risk and other factors to determine if the group is the main responsible person or agent.

### VI Main Taxes

## 1. Enterprise Income Tax

In accordance with the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China, the bank will pay the enterprise income tax at a rate of 25%.

___

## 2. Business Tax

The bank and its subsidiary shall pay the business tax on their taxable turnover at a rate of 5% for the bank and 3% for its subsidiary.

Business tax shall be paid locally where the branches shall declare and pay the tax to the local taxation department.

## 3. Urban Maintenance and Construction Tax

The urban maintenance and construction tax shall be calculated and paid by 1%−7% of the business tax.

4. Educational Surcharge

The educational surcharge shall be calculated and paid by the bank by 3% of the business tax.

## 14. Deferred Income Tax Assets

All subsidiaries of the bank will pay the tax in an aggregate way with relevant deferred income tax assets offset against deferred income tax liabilities and presented in net value; each subsidiary of the bank is seen as independent taxpayer with the relevant deferred income tax assets of the same company offset against deferred income tax liabilities and presented in net value.

The general risk preparation is constituent part of the shareholders' equity, but cannot be used for distribution of dividends. The general risk reserves will be confirmed in the financial condition table when it is approved in the shareholders' general meeting, which is used to make up for our potential losses that has not yet been identified by the bank.

### 30. Profit Distribution

(1) Withdrawal of Legal Surplus Reserve

According to the articles of association, the bank shall withdraw its legal surplus reserve by 10% of the net profit of each year. The bank withdrew RMB80,468 thousand yuan and RMB114,318 thousand yuan as legal surplus in 2014 and 2015 respectively. When the accumulated legal surplus reserve reaches 50% of the registered capital of the bank, it is unnecessary to continue to withdraw the legal surplus reserve.

## (2) Profit distribution implemented in this year

Proposed by the board of directors and approved by the shareholder meeting on June 30 2015, the bank did not withdraw the general risk reserve from 2014 annual net profit in 2015, and did not distribute the cash dividends to the shareholder. The amount of the cash dividends distributed by the subsidiary company of the group in the year of 2015 was 21,850 thousand Yuan, among it, the amount belonging to the cash dividend of the parent company was 11,144 thousand Yuan. The amount of the general risk reserve withdrawn by the subsidiary company in this year was 125 thousand Yuan.

## (3) Profit distribution implemented in last year

Proposed by the board of directors and approved by the shareholder meeting on June 30 2014, the Bank withdrew the general risk reserve from 2013 annual net profit RMB 150,000 thousand Yuan in 2014. This Generic Risk Reserve was made the accounting treatment on December 31, 2014. The cash dividend of RMB 0.80 Yuan (before tax) was distributed for every 10 shares to the shareholders who registered the group up to December 31, 2013. The total amount of the distributed cash dividends was RMB 348,800 thousand Yuan. The amount of the cash dividend distributed to the shareholders by the subsidiary company of the group was 23,000 thousand Yuan in the year of 2014, among it, the cash dividends belonging to the parent company was 11,730 thousand Yuan. The amount of the generic risk reserve withdrawn by the subsidiary company was 5,987 thousand Yuan in this year.

### IX Division Information

The management division is determined according to the internal organizational structure, management requirement and internal reporting system of the group. The board of directors and relevant management committee (main management decision-makers) will regularly review the reports so as to allocate resources to and assess the performance of each division. The main management decision-makers of the group will manage the business and audit the financial information so as to allocate resources and assess performance.

In accordance with the enterprise accounting standard and financial regulations, the assets and liabilities of the divisions as well as the income and performance of the divisions shall be calculated based on the accounting policy of the group. There is no big difference between the accounting policy of the division and the policy for the preparation of financial information.

The transactions between divisions shall be carried out according to general business terms and conditions. The internal expense and transfer pricing shall also be determined by reference to market interests and shall be reflected in the performance report of each division. The interest income and expense incurred from the adjustment to internal expense and transfer price is defined as "interest income/expense among divisions". The interest income and expense acquired from a third party shall be defined as "external interest income/expense".

The income, business performance, assets and liabilities of the divisions include items directly attributable to any division and those distributable items based on reasonable benchmark.

Each branch of the group mainly provides service to local customers in Heilongjiang and very few customers from other regions without largely relying on any single major external customer

The group shall provide customers with the diversified banking and relevant financial services, with each service division described as follows:

#### Corporate Banking Service

Corporate Banking Service Division involves financial products and services provided to all kinds of customers, governmental agencies and financial institutions. These products and services include company loans, trade finance, depositing activities and other various corporate intermediary services.

#### Personal Banking Service

Personal Banking Service Division includes financial products and services provided to individual customers. These products and services include personal loan, deposit products, bank card service, personal financial service and other personal intermediary service.

Capital Management Service

Capital Management Service Division includes currency market transactions or buy–back deal, debt instrument investment service.

##### Other Services

Other Services refer to equity investment and assets, liabilities, income and expense that can not be directly attributable to any division or reasonably distributed.

## XII Transfer of Financial Assets

The Group undertakes repurchase transactions with counterparty. As of December 31,2015, the carrying value of bonds assets and notes assets sold for repurchase was aggregated at RMB 46.923 billion yuan (RMB 3.182 billion yuan as of December 31,2014), with a commitment to repurchase such bonds and notes on some date in the future at predetermined prices. Proceedings from the foregoing bonds and notes was reported as income from financial assets sold for repurchase, the aggregated value of which was RMB 46.146 yuan (RMB 3.122 billion yuan as of December 31,2014). In accordance with the Repurchase Agreement, during the transaction period, the beneficial ownership of the bonds and notes doesn't transfer, and the Group shall not sell or pledge such bonds and notes during the transaction period. Therefore the Group is deemed to retain all or substantial part of the risks and proceedings of the bonds and notes. Therefore the Group determines the bonds and notes as collaterals for loans received from counterparty instead of derecognizing such bonds and notes in the consolidated financial statements. The counterparty's right of recourse is not limited to such transferred assets.

## XIV Financial Risk Management

### 1. Overview

The Group is engaged in banking and other financial services makes the Group exposed to various types of risks. The Group identifies, analyzes, monitors and reports the risk by drawing up risk management policy and setting the risk control. The businesses the Group operates mainly face credit risks, liquidity risks, market risks (exchange rate and interest rate risks) and operational risks.

The goal of the risk management the Group engages in is to obtain appropriate balance between risks and benefits, so as to ensure a safe and stable operation under the reasonable risk level.

### 2. Risk Management Framework

Board of directors of the Bank consists of risk management and the related party transaction control committee. Risk management and the related party transaction control committee is responsible for drawing up the Group's overall risk management and internal controlling strategies; monitoring the Group's risk management; regularly evaluating the overall risk situation, risk tolerance and management ability. Senior management staff of the Group draws up and promotes the implementation of the corresponding risk

management policies, systems and procedures according to the risk management strategies developed by the board of directors. Department of risk management, financial market department and finance department in the bank together make up the main functional departments of the Group's risk management, all of which specifically implementing every policy and regulation of risk management in the Group. Internal audit department of the Group is responsible for the independent review of the Group's risk management and environmental control.

### 3. Credit Risk

#### 3.1 Credit risk management

Credit risk refers to the possible risk of loss due to that the client or counter party fails to perform its obligation. The main credit risk the group faces is originated from the loans and advances issued to the clients and other businesses that face risk inside and outside the balance sheet.

The Group carries out standardized credit management in the whole process of credit business links of credit investigation and reporting, lines of credit review for approval, loan  $ \underline{\text{origination, monitoring}} $ after the loan is issued and non-performing loan management. According to the requirements of guiding principles for classification of loan risks which is published by CBRC, the Group is responsible for the measurement and management of the quality of credit assets.

Except that the credit assets and the deposition of funds of interbank and other financial institutions can bring credit risk to the Group, in terms of the funds business, the Group can refer to available external credit rating information methods to choose interbank with acceptable credit level for management. In addition, the Group can provide financial guarantee business for clients, there is the possibility that the clients will violate the terms of the contract and the Group will make the payment for the clients, and bear a similar risk of loans and advances, so the Group takes equal risk management procedures and policies for this kind of transaction.

#### 3.2 Impairment Appraisal

#### Major factors of impairment appraisal

The Group divides the loans into the following five categories: normal loan, specifically mentioned loan, substandard loans, doubtful loans and loss loans, substandard loans, doubtful loans and loss loans are regarded as the non-performing loans. The main considerations on the impairment of the loans are the possibility to

repay the loan and the recovery of principal and interest of the loan and the major factors of appraisal include: the repayment ability of the borrower, the credit record, the repayment aspiration, the profitability of loan items, warrant or pledge and the legal liability of repaying the loan. The group makes use of the combination assessment or the individual assessment to count and draw the impairment provision of the loans.

The Group appraises the impairment of the loans and advances of the customer at the end of report period according to the accounting policy recorded in Annotation IV. Besides, at the end of report period, the bank analyzes contract sum of the loans and advanced money of the customer and hands it to the management to assess the financial risks.

The definitions of the five categories of the customer's loans and advanced money are lists as follows:

● Normal loan: the borrower can fulfill loans provisions and there is no reasons to doubt that the principal and interest of the loans can not be repaid in full specified amount on time.

● Specially-mentioned loan: though the borrower has the ability to repay the loan at present, there are some factors that may cause adverse impact on the repayment.

● Substandard loan: the repayment ability of the borrower appears obvious problems, and the borrower can not repay the principal and interest of the loan by fully depending on his/her normal operation revenue, that is, though the warrant or pledge is implemented, there are still certain possible losses.

● Doubtful loan: the borrower can not repay the principal and interest of the loan in full specified amount, though the warrant or pledge is implemented, there are still great losses.

● Loss loan: the principal and interest of the loan can not be taken back or only precious little can be taken back even if all the possible measures or the whole necessary legal procedures are carried out.

The accounting policy of the Group to assess the impairment loss of the financial assets is recorded in Impairment of Financial Assets in 7(4) of Annotation IV. n be taken back even if all the possible measures or the whole necessary legal procedures are carried out.

The accounting policy of the Group to assess the impairment loss of the financial assets is recorded in Impairment of Financial Assets in 7(4) of Annotation IV.

3.3 The maximum credit risk exposure information without considering the held pledge or other measures of credit enhancement

At the time of not considering any available pledge or other measures of credit enhancement, the maximum credit risk exposure information reflects the worst case of credit risk exposure of the balance sheet date. The credit risk exposure of the Group and the Bank mainly comes from the loan business and the bond–investment business. Besides, the financial instruments off– balance sheet also have credit risks, such as credit commitment, acceptance bill, letter of guarantee and letter of credit.

Collateral security mainly includes the following types:

● The other individual loans and the company loans and advanced money usually use the land, real estate and other assets of the borrower as the pledge; and

4. Uidity Risk

Liquidity risk is the risk of lack of capital when the debt due. The mismatching of the cash flow of assets and liabilities or deadline may generate the above risk. The liquidity management goal of the group is to make sure there are sufficient funds to meet withdrawals, maturing debt repayments and lending commitments, at the same time, to grasp more new investment opportunities.

Risk Management Department of the Group manages liquidity risk by taking the following means:

● Realize daily funds management through supervising future cash flow;

● Maintain high marketability of asset portfolio so as to sell off rapidly when unexpected cash flow impact happens;

● Supervise asset liquidity ratio so as to meet internal and supervision requirements;

● Maintain stable deposit base; and
